jobs.title: Vice President, Technology and Transformation Risk
jobs.description:
Experience Aviva

Together, we are Aviva.

Our values of Care, Commitment, Community, and Confidence guide how we show up for each other and our customers. At Aviva Canada, we put people first through a culture built on inclusion, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

The Opportunit
y

The VP Technology and Transformation Risk is a senior member of the Canada Risk function, responsible for providing independent second line oversight and challenge across Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks. The role supports the effective management of these risks across Aviva Canada, helping ensure business objectives can be delivered within the Aviva Canada’s risk appetite framework and regulatory expectations.

The role partners closely with Group and local stakeholders to provide independent risk advice, oversight and challenge, supporting the ongoing development of risk management practices and frameworks across technology and transformation activities.

Risks within the role holder's remit include Cyber Risk, Data Risk, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Emerging Technology Risk and other IT risks.

The role leads specialist risk teams and works closely with colleagues across Risk, Technology, Operations and Transformation functions to provide insight on emerging risks, monitor risk exposures, and support consistent application of Aviva Canada and Group policies and standards.

What You'll Do

Provide independent second line oversight and challenge of Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks across the Group.
Partner with senior leaders within Technology, Operations, Customer & Marketing and Transformation functions to support effective risk management and informed decision-making.
Monitor and assess technology and transformation risk exposures, providing insights and recommendations to senior management and risk committees.
Support the development, maintenance and implementation of Aviva Canada and Group risk frameworks, policies, standards and risk appetite measures relating to Technology, Data, Cyber, AI and Transformation risks
Contribute to risk reporting and analysis provided to Board Risk Committee and Executive Committees as required.
Provide independent review and challenge of significant technology and transformation initiatives, including major change programs and strategic investments
Support regulatory engagement activities and the provision of evidence relating to Technology, Cyber, Data and Transformation risk management practices.
Oversee the identification and assessment of technology concentration, critical dependency and third-party risks across key platforms, suppliers and services.
Monitor emerging technology developments and evolving risk trends, providing thought leadership and practical guidance to business stakeholders
Promote consistency in the application of risk policies, frameworks and methodologies across Aviva Canada.
Lead and develop specialist risk teams, creating a high-performance culture and strengthening risk expertise across Technology and Transformation disciplines.
Contribute to the development and execution of the wider Risk Function strategy and priorities.
Support continuous improvement initiatives across the Risk Function, including the adoption of data, technology and agile ways of working.

What You'll Bring

A degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics, Business, or a related field.
15+ years of experience in data governance, data management, analytics, or a related discipline.
Relevant Insurance qualifications and/or Risk professional qualifications, CRM, CRMP, FRM, PRM or equivalent
Significant experience in enterprise risk management within a regulated financial services or insurance environment, including application of the Three Lines of Defense model
Deep expertise in Technology, Cyber, Data, AI, Operational Resilience and Third-Party Risk oversight and governance
Proven oversight of large-scale transformation and change programs, including complex initiatives with multiple stakeholders and dependencies
Experience partnering with senior executives (CIO, COO, business leaders) and influencing strategic decisions
Strong people leadership experience, including building, leading and developing high-performing specialist teams
Experience engaging with regulators, audit functions, executive committees and board-level stakeholders on risk matters.

What You'll Get

Competitive executive compensation package, including annual incentive opportunities.
Comprehensive pension and retirement savings programs.
Flexible hybrid work model.
Industry-leading health and wellness benefits.
Professional development and executive leadership growth opportunities.
Inclusive employee resource groups and diversity initiatives.
Volunteer opportunities and community impact programs.
Competitive vacation and wellness offerings.

jobs.title: Director of Product Management, Data Integrations
jobs.description:
Movable Ink scales content personalization for marketers through data-activated content generation and AI decisioning. The world’s most innovative brands rely on Movable Ink to maximize revenue, simplify workflow and boost marketing agility. Headquartered in New York City with close to 600 employees, Movable Ink serves its global client base with operations throughout North America, Central America, Europe, Australia, and Japan. We’re looking for a Director, Product Management to partner closely with Engineering to define and evolve how data flows across our platform. You’ll lead a team of Senior Product Managers responsible for data workflows and third-party integrations while staying hands-on as a contributor and close partner to Engineering. You’ll have a broad view across our data and integrations ecosystem, connecting the dots between how data arrives from external platforms, how it’s shaped and made useful within our tools, and where it needs to go to power the personalization our customers depend on. You’ll also be a key point of contact for external vendor relationships and a visible, trusted partner to our Partnerships, Sales, and Customer Experience teams. The role reports to the Vice President of Product Management.

Responsibilities

Directly own product initiatives in the data ingestion and standardization space, partnering closely with engineering as a hands-on contributor
Maintain a unified roadmap across a portfolio that spans data ingestion and normalization, event collection and processing, data workflows and orchestration, third-party integrations, and data governance, ensuring investments across these areas connect to broader company priorities including AI, personalization, analytics, and reporting
Serve as a proactive partner to peer product teams who rely on the data platform, bringing them into roadmap decisions early, maintaining visibility into how this team's work affects their products, and contributing informed perspective on platform APIs and developer-facing integration surfaces
Lead, coach, and develop a team of senior product managers across data workflow and integrations domains, with an eye toward each person's distinct growth path
Serve as the senior point of contact for third-party vendor and partner relationships across technical and business development contacts
Support the team in maintaining an active integration pipeline and consistently launching net-new partners that meet adoption and reliability benchmarks
Stay ahead of the evolving marketing technology and data integration landscape, including emerging paradigms such as agentic platforms and Model Context Protocol (MCP)
Be a ruthless advocate for our customers in every interaction and decision

Qualifications

8+ years of product management experience, including people management of senior individual contributors
Deep experience with data products, including ingestion, transformation, normalization, or workflow, and genuine curiosity about how data moves through complex systems
Strong engineering partnership instincts, with fluency in data pipeline architecture, event streaming, ETL/ELT, and data warehouse design sufficient to engage credibly in architectural trade-off conversations
Experience with marketing technology ecosystems including ESPs, MSPs, CDPs, and CRMs, with familiarity with modern data stack technologies such as Snowflake, Kafka, dbt, or Airflow
Working knowledge of API design and developer-facing integration surfaces
A natural coach who can develop people along genuinely different growth paths
Skilled communicator across engineering, commercial, and external partner audiences

The base pay range for this position is $190,000 - $247,000/year, which can include additional bonus depending on the position ultimately offered, in addition to a full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits. The base pay offered may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.
Studies have shown that women, communities of color, and historically underrepresented people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single qualification. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive culture where all Inkers can thrive. If you’re excited about the role but don’t meet all of the abovementioned qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Our differences bring a breadth of knowledge and perspectives that makes us collectively stronger.
We welcome and employ people regardless of race, color, gender identity or expression, religion, genetic information, parental or pregnancy status, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, ethnicity, family or marital status, physical and mental ability, political affiliation, disability, Veteran status, or other protected characteristics. Position Title:
Sr. Director, Digital Technology Commercial Transformation

Position Type:
Regular - Full-Time

Requisition ID:
40323

At McCain, we believe in meaningful technology – using digital technology not just for innovation, but to make a difference globally. Join a team where innovation drives purpose and technology shapes the future. This is your chance to develop sought-after expertise, work on exciting, high-impact projects, and create solutions that truly make a difference. If you're ready to push boundaries, tackle purposeful challenges, and build a career that matters, we want you on our team.

About The Role.

The Sr. Director, Digital Technology Commercial Transformation
is a critical leadership role responsible for developing and guiding a high-performing digital technology team to advance the company’s commercial strategy. This position leads the transformation of marketing, sales, and innovation through the integration of technology, data, and AI. The role collaborates with global and regional leaders to shape strategic plans and roadmaps that drive business growth and efficiency via digital solutions. The Sr Director, Digital Technology Commercial Transformation serves as a change agent and future-oriented strategist, ensuring digital transformation delivers measurable impact on business outcomes, organizational capability, and customer experience.

This senior leadership role requires a strong knowledge of marketing and sales industry-leading approaches for enabling business organizations with digital capabilities. The leader will have a proven track record of successfully delivering digital transformation programs in a Commercial context for a global organization bringing innovative solutions that transform the sales, marketing and innovation processes at McCain.

What You'll Be Doing.

Build trusted relationships and collaborate with stakeholders to define and drive our strategic direction for commercial digital transformation. As a customer-obsessed leader, deliver outcomes that create value for customers and enhance customer experience with McCain.
Work closely with cross-functional and regional leaders to co-create commercial digital enablement roadmaps and deliver digital capabilities that align to achieving our business objectives. Ensure funding, resourcing and outcomes are aligned to the delivery of key initiatives and programs.
Manage an overall portfolio of global and regional initiatives, set priorities, and align with cross-functional teams to successfully deliver value and positive business outcomes. Connect strategy to execution and achieve results as a cohesive team.
Oversee a portfolio of global and regional digital commercial initiatives, ensuring prioritization and delivery of business value. These portfolios include initiatives prioritized in the Sales, Marketing and Innovation commercial roadmaps.
Lead adoption of digital capabilities (both internally as externally with our customers and partners). Measure value and identify future opportunities to continuously enhance our customer experience and drive efficiencies in our ways of working in sales, marketing and innovation.
Manage technology investment plans, budget, forecast, and ensure ROI for digital projects is achieved.
Develop strategic partnerships with industry leading partners to accelerate implementation of our roadmaps. Stay current of industry and technology trends to bring ideas and innovations to McCain.
Proactively address opportunities in the external environment to enhance our future business ambitions with market-leading insights. Lead strategic discussions in Digital Commercial including digital, data & technology capabilities and solutions.
Champion the implementation of best-in-class digital solutions and advocate for process improvement and innovation, including the adoption of AI in commercial functions.
Safeguard the quality and legal compliance of commercial data and applications, in line with data governance standards.
Drive operational excellence for digital commercial solution support and ensure key performance indicators are tracked to measure progress.
Foster a culture of inclusion, accountability, mentorship, and professional development among team members. Lead teams to establish clear vision, create an atmosphere of trust, and inclusion. Coach and mentor team members to learn and develop skills and career experiences.

What You'll Need To Be Successful.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Sciences or equivalent experience, Graduate level desirable (MBA)
10 + years’ experience as a Technology leader, either as a Technology Business Partner for Digital Commercial organizations or as a Digital Leader in a Commercial function.
Proven experience working on large scale technology programs and digital transformation initiatives, preferably in CPG, Food Service, QSR or Retail industries.
Experience leading programs enabled with technologies, specifically in the Digital Commercial space.
Extensive partnership with Commercial stakeholders (both internally and externally).
Solid experience developing and delivering a connected digital and business strategy in a global or large, complex region.
Strong interpersonal skills working at all levels of the organization. Ability to negotiate with both internal and external groups and gain trust to align opportunities for overall success.
Inclusive and inspiring team leadership.

Additional Information.

Connect with external stakeholders as required including participating in customer meetings and industry forums.
Participate in key external relationships with external vendors and industry partners.
Travel: as required.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Momentum Financial Services Group, we help people move forward by reimagining how money works for those who need it most. With more than 40 years of experience, we're the team behind Money Mart—Canada's largest non-bank branch network—and a leader in financial solutions for underserved communities.

From short-term loans to money transfers and prepaid cards, we power the products, technology, and operations that connect over a million customers a year to the money they need, when they need it.

At MFSG, we come together across teams and departments to create something bigger than ourselves: solutions that remove barriers and give people access to money they might not get anywhere else. Whether you're solving problems, building systems, or shaping strategy, your work fuels real support for real people.

We've Got You Covered

Our strategy is designed to attract and retain top talent by offering competitive, fair, and performance-driven rewards. We benchmark against the market, recognize strong performance and continuously evolve to meet the needs of our people and our business.

Discretionary Annual Bonus:
Enjoy the opportunity for a discretionary bonus based on individual performance and company success.

Our benefits include health and dental plans with 100% of the premiums covered. We also offer an Employee Assistance Program to support your mental well-being and provide resources for personal challenges.

Retirement Plans:
Plan for your future with our robust retirement savings options, ensuring you're set for the long haul.

Hybrid Work Environment:
Experience the best of both worlds with our hybrid work model, allowing you to balance remote work with in-office.

Perks and Rewards:
Enjoy reimbursement for tuition assistance and professional development, discounts through Perkopolis and participate in our rewards and recognition programs to celebrate your contributions.

The Job:
Vice President, Data and Enterprise Architecture

What You'll Do

The Vice President, Data and Enterprise Architecture, is responsible for leading Momentum's business and technology on a unified path towards an enterprise target architecture that enables innovation, scalability, and sustainable business growth. This role defines and drives the strategic vision for data, integration, business architecture, and technology platforms —ensuring that architecture and technology investments accelerate business strategy, reduce costs, and position the organization for AI readiness.

What You'll Bring

15+ years of progressive technology leadership in enterprise architecture, data strategy, and platform modernization
Proven experience in rationalizing complex technology environments, reducing technical debt, and delivering measurable cost efficiencies
Demonstrated success leading transformation of large-scale data and technology ecosystems in financial services or similarly regulated industries
Strong track record of building AI- and data-ready enterprise architectures
Experience marrying business architecture with future state architecture

Required Qualifications

Expertise in enterprise data architecture, governance, and analytics
Deep understanding of cloud-native design, integration, and modernization
Strategic ability to balance innovation, performance, and cost optimization
Knowledge of cybersecurity, compliance, and regulatory frameworks
Strong executive communication, influence, and leadership capabilities

Education

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field

Desired Education

Master's degree in Data Science, Cloud Computing, or Enterprise Architecture

Professional Designations (Accreditations, Certificates, Licenses)

Desired Professional Designations

TOGAF or equivalent Enterprise Architecture certification
CISSP / CISM (information security)
AWS, Azure, or GCP Cloud Architecture certifications

If you are selected for an interview, please notify MFSG if you require accommodation in respect of the materials or procedures used at any time during this process. At MFSG, we are committed to building innovative solutions grounded in ethical, transparent, and responsible use of data and technology. Aligned with the principles outlined in Canada's Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA), we take a proactive approach to ensuring that any AI or data-driven systems we use are safe, fair, and accountable.

This posting is for a current position within our organization, offering the opportunity to contribute to meaningful, responsible innovation that supports our employees, clients, and communities.

jobs.description:
SaaS Onboarding -Systems Engineer
& Automation - AVP

Charles River Development is an award-winning provider of software and services to the Investments/Financial Services industry. Our client base includes many of the world’s largest investment and financial institutions. To better serve the growing demand for our Software as a managed service offering.

This is an internal process improvement, business and technical staff position responsible for managing and supporting as an Assistant Vice President (AVP) of Systems & Automation, the candidate will work as conduit within our financial technology ecosystem working with platform engineering, product, SaaS implementation teams. This is not a "maintenance" role; the candidate is expected to be an agent of change. Candidate will scrutinize our existing manual workflows, identify structural gaps, and build the automated bridges necessary to ensure seamless, secure, and rapid software delivery implementing standard SaaS strategy. This AVP position grants the authority to challenge the status quo. The candidate will not just be using the tools but will be working and deciding how to roll out certain functionality on the SaaS platform.

Responsibilities

Audit existing manual processes across the application lifecycle and design/implement automated solutions to eliminate toil.
Develop and maintain robust configuration management scripts using Ansible, Python & PowerShell.
Work with product/engineering teams to optimize the CI/CD pipelines to support rapid, risk-mitigated deployments of CRIMS applications.
Responsible for ensuring efficiency, availability and configuration of the “CRD Development” SaaS platform by providing solutions based on sound technical knowledge.
Adopt, customize and implement industry standard DevOps policies and DevOps procedures.
Create and maintain automated scripts/tools that will build, configure, deploy and test applications deployed to different environments, maintain, support, and enhance continuous integration environments.
Work hands on with the system, installing and configuring it and testing that it meets the product’s technical and business requirements.
Work with an automated release management process for SaaS clients.
Break down moderately complex processes into simple and reliable components.
Proven ability to work autonomously, taking a project from "identified gap" to "automated solution" without constant supervision.

Requirements

Experience in DevOps (or related) technologies.
Knowledge of proficient scripting language using Python or any other object-oriented technologies is must.
Experience with Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, Artifactory, JFrog, Git is mandatory.
Experience with the following is must: Web technologies, databases, server operating systems, servers, networks, job scheduling software, system monitoring software, clusters/high availability systems, Disaster Recovery/Business Continuity etc.
Experience or familiarity with servers and networks is preferred. NoSQL experience is a plus.
Experience with SQL, MS SQL, Oracle Server, PostgreSQL preferred.
Understanding Infrastructure as Service cloud providers such Azure, AWS and Oracle cloud is an advantage.
Knowledge of web technologies and ability to write REST API in python with web framework is advantage.
Ability to use a wide variety of open-source technologies and cloud services.
Experience and knowledge in network protocols (e.g. WINS, DNS, TCP/IP, WinRM, ssh, SFTP, SMTP)
Experience with automation, using scripting and tools like Ansible, Puppet, Chef, RunDeck is added advantage.

Qualifications

Experience: 5+ years in a DevOps, Automation Engineer, or Systems Engineering role, preferably within the Financial Services or Banking sector.
Bachelor’s Degree in technical discipline such as Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics, MIC/CIS, etc.
Understanding of financial application logic and the regulatory rigors of banking production environments.

$90,000 - $157,500 Annual

jobs.title: Interim Vice-President, Psychometrics and Data Analytics
jobs.description:
The Opportunity

The Pharmacy Examining Board of Canada (PEBC), a national not-for-profit certification and assessment body for the pharmacy profession, is seeking an Interim Vice-President, Psychometrics and Data Analytics.

This is a highly strategic executive mandate. PEBC is looking for a strong, proven leader who can redefine its psychometric and data strategies and provide senior leadership across psychometrics, enterprise data strategy, analytics, governance and business intelligence.

Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Senior Management Team, the Interim Vice-President holds overall accountability for psychometrics and related data analysis, and leads PEBC’s enterprise data strategy, data analytics and business intelligence, data governance, and reporting. The role ensures the validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility of high-stakes national certification examinations, and positions data as a strategic asset informing decision-making across the organization.

Combining strategic leadership with deep technical authority, the Interim Vice-President advances psychometric and analytic practice through established and emerging methodologies, research and evidence-informed decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

Oversee the psychometric quality of all assessments, validity, reliability, fairness and defensibility, through test design and administration support, standard setting, equating, scaling, scoring and results reporting.
Ensure consistent application of psychometric methodologies across assessments, in line with professional standards and best practices.
Direct statistical and forensic analyses of examination outcomes, candidate performance and testing incidents (including remote proctoring) to support fair, evidence-based decisions.
Lead the initial development and implementation of an enterprise data governance framework, data quality, integrity, security, privacy, retention, definitions and stewardship, alongside metadata management, a data catalogue, and master and reference data management.
Govern analytical and AI/machine-learning models used in or affecting assessments, including model validation, bias and fairness testing, performance monitoring, drift detection and documentation.
Own the reporting, dashboard and data-visualization environment, including self-serve business intelligence for senior leadership, the Board and stakeholders, underpinned by a governed single source of truth and semantic layer.
Champion a data strategy that treats assessment and operational data as a strategic asset, and advance analytics from descriptive and diagnostic reporting toward predictive and prescriptive capability.
Steward the multi-year data strategy and analytics roadmap aligned to the strategic plan, in collaboration with technology leadership, which owns the underlying data platform and engineering.
Chair the data governance operating model, with named data owners and stewards in each function, reporting through the Senior Management Team to the CEO.

jobs.title: Director of Finance & Administration
jobs.description:
Position Overview

Genome Atlantic
brings businesses, governments, and researchers together to focus expertise and investment on Atlantic Canada’s priorities. We help partners turn insights from DNA into practical solutions that improve health, increase productivity, and drive business growth and job creation. The team at Genome Atlantic is connected by a collaborative way of working and a shared commitment to making an impact across Atlantic Canada. 

We are looking for an experienced finance leader who, working as part of a skilled team, appreciates seeing the impact of what they do.

As our Director, Finance & Administration
, you will be the senior financial leader in the organization and a trusted partner to our President & CEO. This is both a leadership role and a hands-on one. You will provide financial insight and advice, while also being directly involved in the accounting, reporting, budgeting, audit, funding and administrative work that keeps the organization aligned with its commitments and vision.

One day you may be preparing financial information for the Board or advising the CEO on an important decision. The next, you may be collaborating on a project with other Genome Center Finance leads , reconciling financial information, working through a funding claim, coordinating an audit requirement, reviewing a contract or solving an operational issue.

For the right person, that combination of collaborative leadership, variety and hands-on involvement is part of what makes the opportunity interesting.

If you are a CPA who enjoys meaningful work, fostering strong relationships and being part of an experienced team where people know and support one another, we would love to hear from you!

The Opportunity

Reporting to the President & CEO, the Director, Finance & Administration
is responsible for the financial stewardship of Genome Atlantic and the effective administration of across important internal business functions, including:

• accounting, financial management and reporting
• budgeting, forecasting and financial analysis
• funder and project financial management
• external audit and financial controls
• Board and Finance & Audit Committee reporting
• contracts and agreements
• payroll and benefits administration
• selected HR and policy administration
• technology and vendor coordination
• organizational systems and administration

This position has one direct report, the Senior Coordinator, Projects and Finance, and is responsible for providing direction, support and appropriate oversight. The role also works closely with the President & CEO, colleagues, Board members, funders, auditors, project partners and external advisors and contractors.

This role combines strategic financial leadership with hands-on involvement in the day-to-day work. You will contribute directly to Genome Atlantic’s financial and administrative operations, provide trusted advice to the CEO and Board, and help ensure the systems and processes that support the organization are reliable, well managed and effective.

Areas of Responsibility

Financial Leadership & Stewardship

Oversee and work directly within Genome Atlantic’s financial management systems, accounting records, controls and policies; lead budgeting; monitor financial performance; prepare quarterly and annual financial reporting; coordinate the annual audit; and provide financial analysis and advice to support decision-making.

Funding & Project Financial Management

Prepare and oversee financial claims and reporting for funding partners, support project budgeting and financial administration, monitor project financial performance and maintain strong relationships with funders, institutional partners and other Genome Centres.

Board & Governance Support

Prepare and present financial information to the Finance & Audit Committee and Board of Directors and support the President & CEO with the financial and administrative aspects of governance.

Contracts, People & Administration

Work directly with contracts, agreements, payroll and benefits administration, employee documentation, policies, technology and other organizational processes, while coordinating with external professional partners as needed.

Team & Organizational Support

Work collaboratively with an experienced team, share knowledge, strengthen processes and contribute beyond a narrow functional boundary when needed. You will provide direction and support while also valuing the expertise and organizational knowledge of the people around you.

Experience and Qualifications

We are looking for someone who combines strong technical finance expertise with practical business judgement and an approachable, collaborative working style. This includes:

A CPA designation in good standing
A minimum of five years of progressively responsible accounting and financial management experience, including senior-level responsibility for a finance function.
Broad experience across the full financial cycle, including accounting operations, budgeting and forecasting, financial reporting, cash management, financial controls, year-end activities and external audit.
Experience preparing and presenting financial information to senior leaders, Boards and/or Finance and Audit Committees, with the ability to translate financial information into clear, practical advice that supports good decisions.
Experience managing externally funded programs, projects or contribution agreements, including budgets, financial claims, reporting and reconciliation.
Experience building effective relationships with funders, government agencies, institutional partners, auditors and other professional advisors.
Experience supporting, supervising or developing others, with a collaborative approach that respects the knowledge and expertise colleagues bring.
A high level of attention to detail and accuracy, with the discipline to ensure financial information, reporting, records and follow-through are complete, reliable and well managed, while still keeping sight of the bigger picture. 
Experience working effectively with external service providers and professional partners, including accounting and IT support.
Experience with payroll, benefits and confidential employee and compensation information.
Clear communication skills and the ability to build trusted working relationships through responsiveness, dependability and follow-through.
Comfort taking ownership, working independently and knowing when to seek input or involve others.
Comfort moving between strategic advice and hands-on execution, sometimes within the same day.
A practical mindset and an interest in strengthening systems, simplifying processes and helping the organization work effectively.
Flexibility, good humour and a willingness to contribute where needed as part of a small, collaborative team.
Experience with not-for-profit accounting and governance is not required but would be highly valued.
Experience in contract administration, policy or HR administration, research, innovation, academic, government-funded or project-based environments would be an asset.
Strong Microsoft Excel and Microsoft 365 skills are important; experience with QuickBooks would be an asset.

Work Environment

This is a full-time hybrid position based in Halifax, Nova Scotia
.

Genome Atlantic’s current hybrid model includes working in the Halifax office on Tuesday
, Wednesday
and Thursday
, with flexibility to work remotely on Monday and Friday.

Periodic travel within Atlantic Canada and elsewhere in Canada may be required. The role also includes predictable periods of increased activity associated with quarter-end and year-end reporting, audits, funding requirements, Board meetings and project milestones.

Physical Requirements

Ability to sit at a desk or workstation for extended periods of time while performing computer-based work.
Ability to communicate effectively in English with team members, stakeholders, and clients through verbal and written communication.
Ability to travel to other Genome Canada/Genome Centre offices, partner sites, and out-of-province conferences as needed.

How To Apply 

If this role speaks to you, we’d love to hear from you! 

Please share your cover letter and resume as a single PDF (with your full name in the file name) to recruitment@genomeatlantic.ca
with the subject line: Director, Finance and Accounting
.

The application deadline is Monday, October 19th, 2026. 

Individual accommodations due to a disability are available upon request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, religion, ethnicity, gender, disability, citizenship status, marital status, or actual or perceived sexual orientation. 

Genome Atlantic is committed to creating an inclusive environment and building a team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and recognize that experience comes in many forms and skills are transferable. If you feel enthusiastic about our efforts and believe you have the skills to contribute and excel in this role, apply! 

We thank all interested parties; however, only those applicants under consideration will be contacted. 

About Genome Atlantic 

Genome Atlantic connects ideas and people across public and private sectors to fuel innovation and translate discoveries into solutions across key sectors including energy; mining; aquaculture; agriculture and agri-food; forestry; health; and the environment. Together with our many partners, we have enabled over $170 million in strategic R&D since our inception in 2000, driving sustainable economic development in Atlantic Canada’s natural resources, improving health outcomes, enhancing environmental stewardship, and helping our regional industries adapt to climate change. genomeatlantic.ca

Empathetic and learner-centered approach.

‑ First Marketing Strategy: Executing Intelligent Systems for Growth
program from Kellogg Executive Education is an eight-week online experience that prepares leaders to navigate a pivotal shift: AI is redefining how organizations grow and compete.
